name: usePrivateSpace
summary: Whether the app process runs inside Android 15+'s Private Space profile. Existence of the profile is not readable from outside it.
plain: Tells you whether this app instance runs inside the Private Space profile. Android hides the Private Space from other apps and has no public auto-lock setting, so what cannot be read is null and reason says why.
description: A process outside any user profile (UserManager.isProfile() is false) is reported as not inside Private Space. Inside a profile, the user type is read through LauncherApps.getLauncherUserInfo(Process.myUserHandle()) and compared with UserManager.USER_TYPE_PROFILE_PRIVATE (API 35+); when that read is refused isInsidePrivateSpace is null. Android does not list the Private Space profile to third-party apps, so isPrivateSpaceConfigured is true only when the app itself runs inside it and null otherwise. No public API exposes the auto-lock setting, so it is not reported.

returns.name: isInsidePrivateSpace
returns.desc: Whether the current application process runs inside the Private Space profile. False below Android 15 and outside any profile; null when it runs in a profile whose type cannot be read.

returns.name: isPrivateSpaceConfigured
returns.desc: True when the app runs inside the Private Space; null otherwise because Android hides the profile from apps (false below Android 15).

returns.name: reason
returns.desc: Why unreadable values are null; null before the first read.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Error message if private profile querying failed.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: 'hardware' once a read returned isInsidePrivateSpace, 'unavailable' otherwise.

agentNote: Introduced in Android 15 (API 35); below it isInsidePrivateSpace is false and isPrivateSpaceConfigured is false. Do not use isPrivateSpaceConfigured === null to mean 'no Private Space': it means 'not readable'. The auto-lock policy cannot be read and is not part of this hook.
